## Purpose and setup

Iteration 2. The models are kept deliberately simple:

* **Response:** site-mean flux (mean of the two sampling rounds), n = 48.
* **Predictors:** DEM SD, WETprob mean, NDVI mean, CHM mean (raster, `r 10` m
  window) and PRISM annual precipitation. All are standardized (mean 0, SD 1),
  so coefficients are the change in the response per 1 SD of the predictor.
* **CH4 response:** log(CH4 + c), chosen in iteration 1 (Section 2).
* **No random effect:** the ecoregion random intercept is tested in Section 3
  and dropped. Models are ordinary `lm()` fits, which use the same formula
  syntax as lme4 without the `(1 | group)` term.
* **No wetland type:** the production maps have no wetland classes, so type
  can't be used for upscaling.
* **Interactions:** a priori WETprob × NDVI, plus an exploratory screen
  (Section 4).
* **Checks:** residual diagnostics, then spatial autocorrelation in the
  residuals (Section 6).

Exploratory results behind these choices are in `GHG_Raster_EDA.qmd`.

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest) # p-values for lmer fixed effects (Satterthwaite)

## --- Settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
RASTER_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_RasterPredictors.csv")
CLIMATE_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv")
SITES_GPKG <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_all_site_data_GPSupd_6347.gpkg")

WINDOW <- 10 # raster window (m)

## Predictor columns (before standardizing) -> short names used in models
PREDICTORS <- c(
  DEM_sd       = sprintf("DEM_sd_%dm", WINDOW),
  WETprob_mean = sprintf("WETprob_mean_%dm", WINDOW),
  NDVI_mean    = sprintf("NDVI_mean_%dm", WINDOW),
  CHM_mean     = sprintf("CHM_mean_%dm", WINDOW),
  ppt_annual   = "prism_ppt_annual"
)

ASINH_SCALE <- 0.01 # asinh(CH4 / s): linear below ~s, log-like above
SHIFT_ADD <- 0.01 # log / Gamma shift: CH4 + |min(CH4)| + SHIFT_ADD

set.seed(1)

## --- Plot styling (same palette as the EDA notebook) ------------------------
WT_COLS <- c(EM = "#2a78d6", FO = "#eb6834", SS = "#1baf7a")
WT_SHAPES <- c(EM = 16, FO = 17, SS = 15)
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          legend.position = "top")
)
```

## 1. Data

```{r load}
flux_site <- st_read(SITES_GPKG, quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(CH4 = mean(CH4_avg), CO2 = mean(CO2_avg), .groups = "drop")

## PRISM annual normals are the same for both rounds; take the site mean anyway
clim_site <- read.csv(CLIMATE_CSV) |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(prism_ppt_annual = mean(prism_ppt_annual), .groups = "drop")

dat <- read.csv(RASTER_CSV, colClasses = c(huc12 = "character")) |>
  select(Site_ID, Ecoregion, Wetland_Type, x, y, all_of(unname(PREDICTORS[PREDICTORS != "prism_ppt_annual"]))) |>
  left_join(flux_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  left_join(clim_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  rename(all_of(PREDICTORS)) |>
  mutate(
    Ecoregion = factor(Ecoregion),
    Wetland_Type = factor(Wetland_Type, levels = names(WT_COLS)),
    ## standardized copies used in the models: z_<name>
    across(all_of(names(PREDICTORS)), \(v) as.numeric(scale(v)), .names = "z_{.col}")
  )

stopifnot(nrow(dat) == 48, !anyNA(dat))
z_preds <- paste0("z_", names(PREDICTORS))
```

### Predictor collinearity

```{r pred-check}
pred_cor <- cor(dat[names(PREDICTORS)], method = "spearman")
kable(pred_cor, digits = 2, caption = "Spearman ρ among the predictors")

## VIF = diagonal of the inverse correlation matrix
vif <- diag(solve(cor(dat[z_preds])))
kable(tibble(predictor = names(PREDICTORS), VIF = vif), digits = 2,
      caption = "Variance inflation factors (all < 5 is fine)")
```

## 2. CH4 response transformations

CH4 is strongly right-skewed and has a few small negative values, so a plain
log is not possible. Candidates:

| Name | Transform | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| raw | CH4 | reference |
| log shift | log(CH4 + c) | c = \|min\| + `r SHIFT_ADD`; results depend somewhat on c |
| asinh | asinh(CH4 / `r ASINH_SCALE`) | no shift needed; linear near 0, log-like above `r ASINH_SCALE` |
| Gamma | CH4 + c, Gamma GLMM with log link | models the mean on the log scale; no back-transform bias |

```{r transforms}
ch4_shift <- abs(min(dat$CH4)) + SHIFT_ADD

dat <- dat |>
  mutate(
    CH4_shift = CH4 + ch4_shift,
    CH4_log = log(CH4_shift),
    CH4_asinh = asinh(CH4 / ASINH_SCALE)
  )

cat(sprintf("Shift c = %.4f; %d of 48 site means are negative\n",
            ch4_shift, sum(dat$CH4 < 0)))
```

```{r transform-plots, fig.height=6}
tr_long <- dat |>
  select(Site_ID, raw = CH4, `log shift` = CH4_log, asinh = CH4_asinh) |>
  pivot_longer(-Site_ID, names_to = "transform") |>
  mutate(transform = factor(transform, levels = c("raw", "log shift", "asinh")))

h <- ggplot(tr_long, aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "#2a78d6", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~transform, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Site-mean CH4 under each transformation", x = NULL, y = "Sites")

q <- ggplot(tr_long, aes(sample = value)) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  stat_qq(size = 1.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~transform, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Normal Q-Q plots", x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")

h / q
```

```{r transform-table}
tr_long |>
  group_by(transform) |>
  summarise(
    skewness = mean((value - mean(value))^3) / sd(value)^3,
    shapiro_W = shapiro.test(value)$statistic,
    shapiro_p = shapiro.test(value)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Shape of the CH4 response")
```


**Decision (iteration 2):** CH4 is modeled as log(CH4 + c). In iteration 1 it
gave the most normal response and residuals. asinh was similar but slightly
skewed, and a Gamma GLMM on the shifted flux fit poorly (one site 5 SD out).

## 3. Random effect check: is `(1 | Ecoregion)` needed?

Sites were sampled 12 per ecoregion, so ecoregion is the natural grouping. A
random intercept is needed if sites in the same ecoregion have more similar
flux than the predictors explain. The check below fits each model with and
without the random intercept, both by maximum likelihood so their AICs are
comparable. It also reports the ecoregion share of the residual variance.

```{r re-check}
f_ch4 <- as.formula(paste("CH4_log ~", paste(z_preds, collapse = " + ")))
f_co2 <- as.formula(paste("CO2 ~", paste(z_preds, collapse = " + ")))

re_check <- function(f, label) {
  m_lm <- lm(f, data = dat)
  m_re <- lmer(update(f, . ~ . + (1 | Ecoregion)), data = dat, REML = FALSE)
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m_re))
  lrt <- anova(m_re, m_lm)
  tibble(
    response = label,
    ecoregion_var = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Ecoregion"],
    residual_var = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"],
    ecoregion_share = ecoregion_var / (ecoregion_var + residual_var),
    AIC_lm = AIC(m_lm),
    AIC_lmer = AIC(m_re),
    LRT_p = lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
  )
}

bind_rows(re_check(f_ch4, "CH4 (log shift)"), re_check(f_co2, "CO2")) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Ecoregion random intercept: ML fits with and without")
```

The LRT p-value is conservative, because the variance is tested at its
boundary of zero. Halving it is the usual correction.

**Decision:** drop the random effect and fit `lm()` with the same formula.
The basis is the result above, not an assumption that sites within an
ecoregion are independent. Residual similarity at shorter distances (within an
ecoregion) is checked in Section 6. Ecoregion is also a mappable layer, so it
could return later as a fixed effect if residuals show regional structure.

## 4. CH4 model (log shift, `lm`)

### 4.1 Base model

```{r ch4-base}
ch4_base <- lm(f_ch4, data = dat)
summary(ch4_base)
```

```{r coef-fn}
## Coefficient estimates with 95% CIs, one row per term per model
coef_table <- function(models) {
  imap_dfr(models, function(m, nm) {
    ci <- confint(m)
    tibble(model = nm, term = names(coef(m)), estimate = unname(coef(m)),
           lo = ci[, 1], hi = ci[, 2])
  }) |>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    mutate(term = gsub("z_", "", term),
           term = factor(term, levels = rev(unique(term))),
           model = factor(model, levels = names(models)))
}

plot_coefs <- function(ct, title, xlab = "Estimate per 1 SD") {
  ggplot(ct, aes(estimate, term)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, color = "#898781") +
    geom_point(size = 2.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
    facet_wrap(~model) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = "95% confidence intervals", x = xlab, y = NULL)
}
```

### 4.2 Interaction: WETprob × NDVI (a priori hypothesis)

**Hypothesis:** wetter sites with lower vegetation productivity have higher
CH4. In the model this is `WETprob_mean * NDVI_mean`. The hypothesis predicts
a **negative** interaction coefficient: as WETprob rises, the NDVI slope
becomes more negative, so low-NDVI sites stand out most where it is wet.

Two caveats for reading the result:

* At 10 m in summer, low NDVI in a wetland often means open water or bare,
  saturated ground, not only low productivity. NDVI and NDWI are close to mirror
  images here (EDA: ρ ≈ −0.87). So "low NDVI" may partly be a second wetness
  signal.
* WETprob mean is bunched near 1 (see the quantiles below). That leaves little
  spread for an interaction to act on.

```{r wetprob-range}
quantile(dat$WETprob_mean, c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1)) |> round(3)
```

```{r ch4-int}
ch4_int <- lm(update(f_ch4, . ~ . + z_WETprob_mean:z_NDVI_mean), data = dat)
summary(ch4_int)

anova(ch4_base, ch4_int)
c(AIC_base = AIC(ch4_base), AIC_interaction = AIC(ch4_int))
```

```{r int-plot-fn}
## Predicted CH4 vs `x` at low / median / high `mod` (10th, 50th, 90th
## percentiles); other predictors held at their mean (z = 0). Predictions are
## back-transformed to flux: exp(fit) - c (the median, not the mean, flux).
plot_interaction <- function(m, x, mod, title) {
  zx <- paste0("z_", x)
  zm <- paste0("z_", mod)
  q <- quantile(dat[[zm]], c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
  grid <- crossing(!!zx := seq(min(dat[[zx]]), max(dat[[zx]]), length.out = 50),
                   !!zm := q)
  for (p in setdiff(z_preds, c(zx, zm))) grid[[p]] <- 0
  pr <- predict(m, newdata = grid, interval = "confidence")
  grid <- grid |>
    mutate(fit = exp(pr[, "fit"]) - ch4_shift,
           lo = exp(pr[, "lwr"]) - ch4_shift,
           hi = exp(pr[, "upr"]) - ch4_shift,
           xval = .data[[zx]] * sd(dat[[x]]) + mean(dat[[x]]),
           level = factor(.data[[zm]], levels = q,
                          labels = sprintf("%s %s (%.2f)", c("Low", "Median", "High"), mod,
                                           q * sd(dat[[mod]]) + mean(dat[[mod]]))))
  ggplot(grid, aes(xval, fit)) +
    geom_point(data = dat, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = CH4), color = "#c3c2b7", size = 1.8,
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = level), alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(aes(color = level, linetype = level), linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#898781", "#eb6834")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#898781", "#eb6834")) +
    scale_y_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.01),
                       breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = "Other predictors at their mean; grey points = observed site means",
         x = x, y = "CH4 flux (pseudo-log axis)",
         color = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL)
}
```

```{r int-plot, fig.height=5}
plot_interaction(ch4_int, "NDVI_mean", "WETprob_mean",
                 "Predicted CH4 vs NDVI at low, median and high WETprob")
```

### 4.3 Other candidate interactions (exploratory)

These interactions also have an ecological rationale. Each is added to the base
model **one at a time**:

| Interaction | Rationale |
|---|---|
| WETprob × DEM_sd | Wet, flat ground is saturated evenly; on wet ground with hummocks and hollows, CH4 depends on microtopography |
| WETprob × CHM_mean | Separates open wet sites (marsh, fen) from wet forested sites (swamp); open, wet sites are expected to emit more |
| WETprob × ppt_annual | A wet landscape in a wetter climate stays saturated longer |
| DEM_sd × ppt_annual | Microtopography matters more where water supply is limited |
| NDVI × CHM_mean | Productive herbaceous cover (high NDVI, low canopy) vs forest |

With n = 48 and five main effects, the model can only support one or two
interactions. Taking the best of several also overstates its evidence: with
six candidates, one p ≈ 0.05 is close to what chance alone produces.
**Treat this table as hypothesis-generating.** Any interaction carried forward
should be checked with cross-validation, not only its p-value.

```{r int-screen}
candidates <- c(
  "WETprob × NDVI"       = "z_WETprob_mean:z_NDVI_mean",
  "WETprob × DEM_sd"     = "z_WETprob_mean:z_DEM_sd",
  "WETprob × CHM_mean"   = "z_WETprob_mean:z_CHM_mean",
  "WETprob × ppt_annual" = "z_WETprob_mean:z_ppt_annual",
  "DEM_sd × ppt_annual"  = "z_DEM_sd:z_ppt_annual",
  "NDVI × CHM_mean"      = "z_NDVI_mean:z_CHM_mean"
)

int_models <- map(candidates, \(trm) lm(update(f_ch4, as.formula(paste(". ~ . +", trm))), data = dat))

imap_dfr(int_models, function(m, nm) {
  cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  row <- cf[grepl(":", rownames(cf)), , drop = FALSE]
  tibble(interaction = nm, estimate = row[1, 1], p = row[1, 4],
         dAIC = AIC(m) - AIC(ch4_base),
         R2 = summary(m)$r.squared, adj_R2 = summary(m)$adj.r.squared)
}) |>
  add_row(interaction = "(base, no interaction)", estimate = NA, p = NA, dAIC = 0,
          R2 = summary(ch4_base)$r.squared, adj_R2 = summary(ch4_base)$adj.r.squared,
          .before = 1) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "CH4 base model plus one interaction (dAIC < 0 = better than base)")
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### WETprob × DEM_sd

```{r int-dem, fig.height=5}
plot_interaction(int_models[["WETprob × DEM_sd"]], "DEM_sd", "WETprob_mean",
                 "Predicted CH4 vs DEM SD at low, median and high WETprob")
```

#### WETprob × CHM_mean

```{r int-chm, fig.height=5}
plot_interaction(int_models[["WETprob × CHM_mean"]], "CHM_mean", "WETprob_mean",
                 "Predicted CH4 vs CHM mean at low, median and high WETprob")
```

:::

### 4.4 Coefficients and diagnostics

```{r ch4-models}
ch4_models <- list(
  base = ch4_base,
  `+ WETprob × NDVI` = ch4_int
)
```

```{r ch4-coefs, fig.height=4.5}
plot_coefs(coef_table(ch4_models), "CH4 (log shift): coefficients",
           "Estimate per 1 SD (log scale; exp(b) = multiplicative change)")
```

```{r diag-fn}
## Residuals vs fitted and normal Q-Q, models side by side
diag_plots <- function(models) {
  d <- imap_dfr(models, \(m, nm) tibble(
    model = nm, fitted = fitted(m), resid = residuals(m),
    Wetland_Type = dat$Wetland_Type
  )) |>
    mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(models)))
  rf <- ggplot(d, aes(fitted, resid)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
    geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
    scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
    labs(title = "Residuals vs fitted", x = "Fitted", y = "Residual",
         color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
  qq <- ggplot(d, aes(sample = resid)) +
    stat_qq_line(color = "#c3c2b7") +
    stat_qq(size = 1.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
    facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = "Residual normal Q-Q", x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")
  rf / qq
}
```

```{r ch4-diag, fig.height=7}
diag_plots(ch4_models)
```

Wetland type is not in the model, because it can't be mapped. Colouring the
residuals by type shows whether the predictors already capture the differences
between types.

## 5. CO2 model

CO2 is roughly symmetric and includes many negative values (uptake), so it is
modeled untransformed with the same predictors.

```{r co2-fit}
co2_models <- list(base = lm(f_co2, data = dat))
summary(co2_models$base)
```

```{r co2-coefs, fig.height=3.5}
plot_coefs(coef_table(co2_models), "CO2: coefficients")
```

```{r co2-diag, fig.height=6}
diag_plots(co2_models)
```

## 6. Spatial autocorrelation in residuals

Sites cluster in space (the nearest neighbour is a median of ~14 km away, and a
few pairs are under 1 km apart). If nearby sites have similar residuals, the
model's standard errors are too small. Two checks:

* **Moran's I.** I near 0 means no spatial pattern; positive I means nearby
  residuals are alike. The p-value comes from 999 random permutations of the
  residuals among sites (one-sided, testing for positive autocorrelation). Two
  weightings are shown:
    * **Neighbours within `r 25` km** (main test): every site pair closer than
      25 km counts equally.
    * **Inverse distance**: weights are 1/distance, so the handful of site
      pairs under 1 km dominate. This can give a very different answer from
      the band test.
* **Correlogram:** Moran's I for site pairs within distance bands, to see at
  what distance any similarity fades.

```{r moran-fn}
dist_km <- as.matrix(dist(dat[c("x", "y")])) / 1000

moran_I <- function(r, w) {
  z <- r - mean(r)
  length(r) / sum(w) * sum(w * outer(z, z)) / sum(z^2)
}

moran_test <- function(r, w, nsim = 999) {
  obs <- moran_I(r, w)
  sims <- replicate(nsim, moran_I(sample(r), w))
  tibble(I = obs, expected = -1 / (length(r) - 1),
         p = (sum(sims >= obs) + 1) / (nsim + 1)) # one-sided: positive autocorrelation
}

NEIGHBOUR_KM <- 25

w_band <- (dist_km <= NEIGHBOUR_KM) * 1
diag(w_band) <- 0
w_inv <- 1 / dist_km
diag(w_inv) <- 0

BANDS_KM <- c(0, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, Inf)

correlogram <- function(r) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(length(BANDS_KM) - 1), function(i) {
    w <- (dist_km > BANDS_KM[i] & dist_km <= BANDS_KM[i + 1]) * 1
    diag(w) <- 0
    tibble(band = sprintf("%g–%g km", BANDS_KM[i], BANDS_KM[i + 1]),
           n_pairs = sum(w) / 2) |>
      bind_cols(moran_test(r, w))
  }) |>
    mutate(band = factor(band, levels = band))
}

cat(sum(w_band) / 2, "site pairs within", NEIGHBOUR_KM, "km;",
    sum(rowSums(w_band) > 0), "of 48 sites have at least one neighbour\n")

all_models <- c(setNames(ch4_models, paste("CH4", names(ch4_models))),
                setNames(co2_models, paste("CO2", names(co2_models))))
model_resid <- map(all_models, residuals)
```

```{r moran-table}
bind_rows(
  map_dfr(model_resid, \(r) moran_test(r, w_band), .id = "model") |>
    mutate(weights = sprintf("within %d km", NEIGHBOUR_KM)),
  map_dfr(model_resid, \(r) moran_test(r, w_inv), .id = "model") |>
    mutate(weights = "inverse distance")
) |>
  select(model, weights, I, expected, p) |>
  arrange(model) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Moran's I of model residuals")
```

```{r correlogram, fig.height=4}
corr_res <- map_dfr(model_resid, correlogram, .id = "model") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(model_resid)))

ggplot(corr_res, aes(band, I, group = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -1 / 47, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_line(color = "#898781") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_pairs, shape = p < 0.05), color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, name = "Site pairs") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 16), name = "p < 0.05") +
  labs(title = "Residual correlogram", subtitle = "Grey line = expected I with no autocorrelation",
       x = "Distance band", y = "Moran's I") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

corr_res |>
  filter(BANDS_KM[as.integer(band)] < 50) |>
  select(model, band, n_pairs, I, p) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Correlogram, bands under 50 km")
```

Bands with few site pairs (small points) are noisy; focus on the short bands.

```{r resid-map, fig.height=6}
imap_dfr(model_resid, \(r, nm) tibble(model = nm, x = dat$x, y = dat$y,
                                      resid_z = as.numeric(scale(r)))) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(model_resid))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x / 1000, y / 1000, fill = resid_z)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, color = "white", stroke = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#e34948",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-2.5, 2.5), oob = scales::squish,
                       name = "Residual (SD)") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Residuals in space", subtitle = "Colour capped at ±2.5 SD",
       x = "Easting (km, EPSG:6347)", y = "Northing (km)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## 7. Next steps

* **Spatial autocorrelation in CH4 residuals.** If the 0–25 km signal holds, the
  options from least to most complex are:
    * a random intercept for a spatial group defined at that scale, for example
      sites clustered within ~25 km (`(1 | site_group)` in lme4);
    * a spatial correlation structure (`nlme::gls` with `corExp`); or
    * spatially blocked cross-validation, so predictive skill is not overstated.
* **Interactions.** Decide whether any interaction from Section 4.3 is worth
  carrying forward, and test it with cross-validation.
* **Predictive check.** Use leave-one-out or spatially blocked cross-validation
  to see how well the models predict sites they were not fitted on.

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
